title: Alibi and Cipher
premise: Wren Ashgrove, coroner of the coastal town of Saltmere, receives a confession letter for a drowning ruled accidental thirty years ago — postmarked the day after the victim's sister is finally buried beside him. As Wren investigates, he discovers the letter was written by his own late mentor, the former coroner who signed the original death certificate, and that half the town's founding families are entangled in the cover-up. The truth surfaces with the winter tide: the victim's death was an accident, but the alibi that protected one boy from blame destroyed another man's life, and Wren must choose between publishing the truth and preserving the fragile belonging of a town that took him in. He chooses truth — but delivers it privately, grave by grave, letting the living decide what to do with it.
about_author: Astrid Underhill is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing coroners' inquest records from small coastal towns before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about the paperwork of death and the people who keep it.

chapters.title: Postmark
chapters.summary: Wren Ashgrove's POV. Days after burying Maren Voss, Wren finds a confession letter among her effects, unsigned, admitting to a thirty-year-old drowning. The emotional beat is unease: he knows every file in his office, and this death was closed long before his time. He begins pulling the old records against his better judgment.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, with flashbacks to his arrival in Saltmere seven years ago as a grieving outsider. He reconstructs the original inquest and finds his mentor Edith Crane's signature on a certificate that contradicts the tide charts. The beat is loyalty tested — Edith trained him, and questioning her feels like betrayal.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV introducing Denny Voss, Maren's brother, who returned to town for her funeral and won't leave. He claims Maren received letters too. Wren realizes someone has been paying the family quietly for decades. The beat is suspicion tightening around Saltmere's founding families.

chapters.title: Three Alibis
chapters.summary: Wren interviews the three surviving witnesses from that night: harbor master Colm Pike, teacher Ruth Ellery, and patriarch August Hale. Each gives a polished, rehearsed alibi — too polished. The beat is dread; Wren recognizes coached testimony because he's heard it across a hundred death tables.

chapters.title: Edith's Hand
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Handwriting analysis confirms the confession is Edith Crane's, written shortly before her death two years ago and mailed on a delay by an unknown hand. He searches her sealed estate and finds a second document: not a confession of murder, but of falsification. The beat is vertigo — the ground under his profession shifts.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Denny's POV. Flashback structure reveals a fourth person on the dock that night: a foster kid named Tobias, who vanished from town records entirely. Denny remembers him; no one else will say his name. The beat is grief for the erased — identity as something the town can grant or revoke.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Following Edith's notes, he finds Tobias alive under a changed name, living two towns over, broken by exile. Tobias confesses what really happened: an accident, a panic, and a deal — his silence purchased with banishment while Hale's son kept his future. The beat is fury and pity intertwined.

chapters.title: Pressure
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. Someone ransacks Wren's office; Ruth Ellery begs him to stop; August Hale offers him Edith's old position and a place that finally feels like belonging. The beat is temptation at its strongest — Wren understands now why Edith signed the certificate, and how easily he could sign the next one.

chapters.title: The Turning Tide
chapters.summary: Climax. Wren's POV. Confronting Hale at the dock on the storm anniversary, Wren lays out the full chain: the accident, the falsified certificate, the payments, the erasure. Hale's son — now the town's doctor — arrives and confesses publicly rather than let his father bury one more truth. The beat is catharsis through surrender.

chapters.title: Grave by Grave
chapters.summary: Resolution, Wren's POV. No arrests — the statute has run, and the town must live with itself instead. Wren files a corrected addendum to the inquest, restores Tobias's name to the record, and visits each involved family privately with the truth. The final image: Wren at the graves, no longer alphabetizing secrets but reading them aloud. The beat is belonging earned honestly.
